title: Microsoft Stock (MSFT) Rises 2.7% as AI Cloud Stocks Rally (Nov 3)
summary: Microsoft (MSFT) rose 2.74% to $520.99 on Nov 3 as AI cloud stocks rallied after Oracle's $20 billion stock and bond sale. How the session traded.
body_markdown:
## Why Microsoft Stock Rose


No source covering the session tied the November 3 gain to a Microsoft announcement, so the move is best read against its AI peers and the indices. Late on November 2, Oracle announced it had priced $20 billion of common stock and senior notes, split equally between stock and bonds, according to[24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/03/oracle-rallies-6-as-20-billion-stock-and-bond-sale-clears-funding-overhang-coreweave-climbs-7-microsoft-gains-2/) , which reported that the sale spooked investors one day and rallied them the next.


The same report said CoreWeave's bigger move outpaced Microsoft's gain, signaling "broader AI cloud optimism, not an Oracle-only story." It also noted that Oracle databases run inside Microsoft Azure through a multicloud partnership.


Per[The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/11/03/stock-market-today-nov-3-markets-edge-higher-as-semiconductor-stocks-rebound/) , semiconductor stocks rebounded and tech stocks broke their recent losing streak on Tuesday, while the[US midterm elections](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/midterms-apple-palantir-and-amd-tonight/) took a back seat to earnings in a mixed session.


## MSFT Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- According to[Microsoft's fiscal 2027 first-quarter release](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/fy-2027-q1/press-release-webcast) of October 28, commercial remaining performance obligation increased 73% to $677 billion.
- The same[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) showed revenue of $92.3 billion, up 19%, Microsoft Cloud revenue up 30% to $63.9 billion, and Azure revenue up 48%.
- 24/7 Wall St. noted that Microsoft spreads its AI spending across a broad base of software, productivity tools and Azure cloud services.


### Risks


- Microsoft's additions to property and equipment reached $39.4 billion in the quarter, per its release, while The Motley Fool said investors remain cautious about AI valuations and revenue generation.
- 24/7 Wall St. reported that JPMorgan said a Democratic sweep in this fall's elections could trigger a selloff in AI stocks, while Bernstein argued the political risk to US data center builds may be overstated.
